newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold exchange to launch futures on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold exchange to launch futures on Friday.

text.p: The Istanbul gold exchange is to launch a gold futures market on Friday, bourse officials said on Wednesday.
It will be the first futures market in Turkey.
Trading in lira or dollar based gold future contracts will take place between 1100 and 1600 local time (0800-1300 GMT) when the exchange's spot gold market is open.
The size of futures contracts will be three kg and the maximum expiry periods will be six months for deals conducted in lira terms and of one year for dollar based deals.
Initially, the gold futures market will start with 30 members, including 17 banks, seven foreign exchange and gold offices, three precious metal brokerages and three stock market brokerages.

The members will pay guarantees to the Exchange to be able to conduct transanctions and settlements in the market and can get a maximum commission fee of 0.001 percent of the contract value from their customers.
A member can hold a maximum of 1,000 futures contracts for itself and its customers for a certain delivery date and 5,000 in total at any time.
A customer can buy a maximum of 100 futures contracts for a certain delivery date and a maximum of 250 in total at any time.
Initially, 12 members, including 10 banks were authorised to carry out futures contract settlements on behalf of their customers and other members as well as for their own contracts.
The remaining 18 members can only settle contracts of their own.
